s1.syndrome_frame: Jaw pain and tooth mobility with radiographic evidence of a unilocular radiolucent lesion
salient_findings: Tender percussion of the right mandibular second premolar and first molar
Slight mobility of the affected teeth
Buccolingual expansion with cortical thinning on cone beam CT
key_facts: 34-year-old woman presented with jaw pain
Pain and slight mobility of the mandibular right second premolar and first molar
Tender percussion of both teeth
Slight mobility of the affected teeth
Normal overlying mucosa and skin
No erythema, ulceration, or warmth
Bony-hard consistency of the buccal and lingual cortices
Mucosal integrity intact
Unilocular radiolucent lesion on orthopantomogram
Lesion engulfing the apices of the right mandibular second premolar and first molar
Lesion extending to the superior border of the inferior alveolar nerve canal
Irregular shape of the lesion atypical for routine periapical cysts or granulomas
Buccolingual expansion with almost complete obliteration of the lingual cortex on cone beam CT
Lesion measuring approximately 23.4 × 14.2 × 6.6 mm

shortlist.label: Odontogenic keratocyst
shortlist.why_kept: Unilocular radiolucent lesion with buccolingual expansion and irregular shape

shortlist.label: Unicystic ameloblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Radiographic findings of a unilocular radiolucent lesion with buccolingual expansion

shortlist.label: Radicular cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Tender percussion and slight mobility of the affected teeth

shortlist.label: Keratocystic odontogenic tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Similar radiographic appearance to odontogenic keratocyst

shortlist.label: Dentigerous cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of jaw pain and tooth mobility

shortlist.label: Aneurysmal bone cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely, could present with similar radiographic findings

shortlist.label: Simple bone cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Could be considered due to the presence of a unilocular radiolucent lesion

shortlist.label: Giant cell granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Although rare, could be a possible cause of jaw pain and tooth mobility

raw.rationale: The presence of a unilocular radiolucent lesion with an irregular shape, buccolingual expansion, and almost complete obliteration of the lingual cortex, along with the patient's age and the location of the lesion, are consistent with the characteristics of an odontogenic keratocyst, now more commonly referred to as a keratocystic odontogenic tumor.

rejected.label: Radicular cyst
rejected.why: The irregular shape of the lesion and its extension beyond the apices of the involved teeth are atypical for a radicular cyst.

rejected.label: Unicystic ameloblastoma
rejected.why: While possible, the lack of specific mention of characteristic ameloblastoma features such as a unilocular radiolucency with scalloped borders or the presence of an impacted tooth makes this less likely.

rejected.label: Keratocystic odontogenic tumor
rejected.why: This is essentially the same entity as the odontogenic keratocyst, with the term keratocystic odontogenic tumor being a more recent classification.

rejected.label: Dentigerous cyst
rejected.why: The absence of an impacted tooth associated with the lesion makes this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Aneurysmal bone cyst
rejected.why: Typically presents with more aggressive features such as rapid growth and significant bone expansion, which are not prominently described in this case.

rejected.label: Simple bone cyst
rejected.why: Usually presents as a well-defined radiolucency without the significant buccolingual expansion seen in this case.

rejected.label: Giant cell granuloma
rejected.why: Typically has a more aggressive radiographic appearance with multiple radiolucencies and is less likely given the description of a single unilocular lesion.
